title: Exporter canary funnel and vendor sanity suite for tracing backends
creator: Maya Thompson
description:
Goal:
Build a repeatable canary funnel and automated sanity test suite that validates OpenTelemetry/OTLP exporters and downstream wiring to vendor tracing backends (Tempo, Jaeger, Tempo-as-a-service vendors). This is intended to catch integration regressions introduced by runtime changes (collector config, header propagation, batching/backpressure behavior, retry semantics) before they reach customer-facing ingests.

Scope:
- Canary funnel (staging) that replays synthetic trace traffic into the same code paths as production (ingest path + exporter).
- Vendor sanity suite that executes a set of deterministic checks against a target backend endpoint: span arrival, ordering, parent/traceid consistency, sampling tag preservation, header-based tenant mapping, and idempotent replay behavior.
- CI gates: run lightweight vendor sanity on PRs that touch exporter/collector code; nightly canaries to validate long-tail behavior and flaky network scenarios.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Canary job deployed to staging that sends 5k synthetic traces per day across 3 trace shapes (short chat, long generation, async worker) and reports exporter success rate and P50/P95 export latency to the console dashboard.
2) Vendor sanity suite with 12 checks (listed below) that can be executed locally (docker-compose) and in CI against a vendor endpoint using a credentials fixture.
3) Failures produce actionable telemetry: exporter error class (auth/4xx/5xx/timeout), dropped-span counts, and a link to a minimal failing trace in Tempo/Jaeger UI.
4) Playbook added to Confluence describing troubleshooting steps and rollback/mitigation (fallback routing to compatible model variant).

Sanity checks included:
- Trace acceptance: verify spans with the same trace_id arrive within expected time window and maintain parent relationships.
- Order preservation: consecutive spans maintain increasing timestamps for single-threaded traces.
- Sampling tag preservation: original sampling decision attribute preserved in vendor storage.
- Header propagation: tenant and routing headers forwarded and acknowledged by backend (tenant id present in saved span label).
- Retry idempotency: replays do not create duplicate logical traces (use deterministic span ids and idempotency keys).
- Backpressure behavior: exporter responds to backend 429 with exponential backoff and no unbounded memory growth.
- TLS/mTLS handshake validation and cert rotation handling.
- Envelope compression: validate compressed payloads accepted and decompressed properly.
- Attribute size trimming: oversized attribute behavior consistent with documented policy.
- Auth token rotation: validate exporter rotates credentials without dropping inflight batches.
- Latency histogram: p50/p95 export latency within SLO for staging.
- Dead-letter behaviour: verify messages sent to DLQ on persistent 5xx and surfaced in console.

Design decisions / trade-offs:
- We will emulate vendor endpoints locally with lightweight Tempo/Jaeger containers and a HTTP proxy that can inject faults. This reduces remote vendor cost and lets us run CI checks offline; however, it may miss vendor-specific quirks. To mitigate, nightly canaries will run against a small sample of real vendor endpoints (credentials managed in vault).
- Keep the CI-level sanity checks lightweight (fast deterministic checks) and push heavier, non-deterministic tests to the nightly pipeline to avoid PR latency.
- Prefer black-box checks (behavioral) over deep coupling to vendor internals to reduce maintenance burden when vendors change storage internals.

Implementation plan:
- Week 1: prototype local harness with dockerized Tempo and Jaeger, plus a fault-injecting proxy; basic synthetic trace generator (node/python) and small CI job.
- Week 2: extend sanity checks, add exporter metrics exporters (success_count, error_class, export_latency), and wire metrics to console dashboard.
- Week 3: integrate canary scheduler in staging, add vault-backed vendor credentials, and create Confluence playbook.
- Week 4: CI gate rollout and handoff to oncall/product for runbook review.

Artifacts & links:
- Design doc (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/Exporter+Canary+Funnel
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4821
- Local harness repo (internal): https://github.com/redwood-inference/trace-canary-harness (README contains docker-compose and test vectors)
- Console dashboard (staging): https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/trace-exporter-canary

Open questions:
- Which vendor endpoints should be included in the nightly sample (we should pick 2 managed vendors + 1 self-hosted Tempo cluster)?
- Should we surface exporter-level debug logs in the console by default or keep them gated behind an opt-in?

Next steps:
- Jamal to land prototype harness PR and confirm docker images for Tempo/Jaeger.
- Maya to create the Confluence playbook skeleton and list required vault secrets.
- Schedule a 30m sync with Platform-oncall to review the playbook and escalation flow.
